A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TVE framework and retain matching main experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RelBench experiments, including downstream performance, linear probing, sensitivity analyses and measured pre-training runtimes.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original noise, cross-entity transfer, Seznam cell-prediction and task-vector construction measurements.

M1.justification: The documented TVE procedure retains its cross-joined pre-training table, causal schema traversal, SQL statistics, scaled cosine loss and optional SSL hybrid objective. The breadth-first traversal explanation and fuller aggregator list clarify the existing procedure; learnable set encoders remain future work.

E1.justification: Appendix C.7 adds Seznam/charge, predicting the sluzba attribute of dobito rows. This extends evaluation beyond the retained rel-amazon and rel-hm forecasting tasks to a new database and cell-level prediction requirements.

E2.justification: Corresponding original comparisons retain the unpretrained Baseline, GraphMAE-derived MAE and GraphCL-derived CTR methods. The added experiments reuse these comparators. Cross-entity TVE configurations are transfer controls, while newly cited methods such as Griffin are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols generate labels after dropping 20% or 40% of review rows while retaining the original graph for model inputs, and test transfer between item- and user-pretrained representations. Seznam adds dated validation/test cutoffs and Accuracy, Macro F1, Micro F1 and MRR evaluation under linear probing and fine-tuning. Original RelBench settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C.5–C.6 add controlled tests of dependence on graph-derived labels and transfer across entity types, addressing robustness and representation specificity beyond v1's sensitivity studies. Appendix C.9.1 also adds construction-time and peak-memory profiling. Existing learning-rate and initialization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports repeated runs and ± values; v2's checklist item 7 newly identifies the reported quantities as means and standard deviations. The stated repetition counts for retained experiments are unchanged, with no documented increase in runs or new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Original numerical tables and plotted results are retained, while Tables 7–10 add noise, transfer, cell-prediction and construction-cost results. For example, new Seznam test accuracies are 69.90 for TVE-1 versus 70.52 for MAE-0.25 under linear probing, and 81.26 versus CTR-0.25's 81.31 after fine-tuning. These are newly evaluated conditions, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: Appendix C.9.1 introduces Remark C.1 and a derivation of construction complexity O(rNTp^k b^k). Appendix D.2 adds mathematical arguments about sufficient statistics and reconstruction of small multisets. Theorem 4.1 and its proof remain unchanged; the full label-generation equations moved to Appendix B are not new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims about TVE, task-relevant information preservation and downstream benefits, especially with limited labels. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of robustness to label/graph mismatch, the benefit of matching pre-training and downstream entity types, and applicability to fact-table cell prediction. Appendix D substantially develops the tradeoff between fixed statistics and learnable set encoders, while C.9 explains exponential traversal costs. These extend v1's brief limitations discussion.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a public-code URL, explicitly lists numerical and categorical SQL aggregators, and documents construction time and peak memory. It also specifies Seznam task creation through AutoCompleteTask and dated split cutoffs. These materially expand reproducibility information; existing hardware, training schedules and hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to mutual information neural estimation, the CTU Prague relational repository, Griffin and Deep Sets. These support dataset attribution and the expanded statistics discussion. The main related-work section and TVE's positioning relative to existing SSL approaches remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted explanatory edits concerning decoder roles, traversal and notation, moving the full label-generation notation into Appendix B. It adds acknowledgements and a conference checklist and reorganizes supplementary sections. The main narrative and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands tabular presentation with separate displays for noise experiments, entity transfer, four-metric cell prediction and construction resources (Tables 7–10). Existing figures are retained. Legacy tables are relocated and renumbered, including v1 Table 5 becoming v2 Table 3 and v1 Table 7 becoming v2 Table 11.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1's robustness, transfer and applicability evidence through Appendices C.5–C.7. Construction-cost analysis also makes scalability assessable beyond v1's per-step timings. Mixed Seznam performance and substantial two-hop memory requirements help reveal practical boundaries. Together with fuller implementation documentation and a code pointer, these additions substantially strengthen evidential coverage and transparency, although the idealized sufficiency assumptions remain.
